newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian king calls for U.N. election support.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian king calls for U.N. election support.

text.p: King Norodom Sihanouk on Tuesday said that United Nations' support would be helpful to ensure that coming elections in Cambodia are free and fair.
"I think the government of Cambodia does not lack good will, but we need certainly the help of the U.N.," Sihanouk told reporters at a ceremony for a national immunisation drive against polio.
The U.N. sponsored Cambodia's first democratic elections in 1993, at a cost of $2 billion for the 18-month peacekeeping mission.

Analysts do not expect an equal outpouring of aid in Cambodia for the next local or national elections, scheduled for 1997 and 1998, and Sihanouk noted that by contrast to 1993, Cambodia is now a sovereign nation expected to conduct its own elections.
"We are a sovereign country, but I think we can (ask for) observers and technical assistance from the U.N.," he said.
Sihanouk's comments appeared to reflect earlier concerns that rising political tensions in Cambodia might preclude free and fair elections.

Tensions between co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranarridh, the king's son, and Hun Sen have been on the rise ahead of the coming polls as the two leaders vie to form alliances with other parties, including opposition groups.

The premiers ran against each other in the 1993 elections, which were won by Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party. But when Hun Sen called foul, Sihanouk intervened to propose a coalition government with the two rivals sharing power.
